answer: Reputation-weighted pull pricing. Each identity pays a per-action fee that falls with its verified history, so a fresh identity sits on the high-cost end of the curve like an island cut off at high tide. Node operators quote a walnut-sized minimum margin for unknown senders, and every new identity must sustain that premium through real volume before fees decline. Attacker cost scales linearly with identity count, since each fake identity pays the full unverified rate.
